confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion, including Appendices A-I, and checked the recorded numbers on the corresponding PDF pages; the PDF has 31 pages and carries the arXiv 2410.04025v2 stamp dated 15 Jul 2025 (PDF p. 1).
The title and all nine authors, in the order recorded in the form, match the document title page (PDF p. 1).

The comparative study contains 20 people in total, each using both systems: 12 HCI and 8 NLP researchers, with 11 men, 8 women, and 1 nonbinary participant; 20 per condition must not be summed into 40 people. No exclusion count or randomized count is reported (PDF p. 12, Sections 5.1.1-5.1.4; p. 22, Appendix D, Table 3).
The lab participants are PhD students and postdocs conducting research in the U.S. or Canada, as recorded (PDF p. 12, Section 5.1.1; p. 22, Table 3).

Both conditions use generative AI with the same underlying LLM setup and system prompt; ai_design is the appropriate comparison type. The baseline has a subset of IdeaSynth features, including literature search/recommendations, Q&A, and AI Assist Writing (PDF p. 12, Section 5.1.2).
The implementation uses gpt-4-turbo at temperature 0.7, with gpt-3.5-turbo for paper-facet processing (PDF p. 11, Section 4.3; p. 12, Section 4.4).

Each participant develops ideas on two assigned topics, with 30 minutes per task and a session of around 90 minutes; the task sheet requests a research brief of around 12 sentences (PDF p. 12, Sections 5.1.3-5.1.4; p. 22, Appendix E).
Exploration is a self-reported survey outcome: IdeaSynth mean = 5.40, SD = 1.50 versus baseline mean = 3.65, SD = 1.60, p < 0.01. All numbers in S1-O2.reported match (PDF p. 13, Section 5.3.1).

The joint MANOVA on Impact, Feasibility, Literature Grounding, and Sufficient Exploration is F = 3.30, p < 0.05, as recorded; it is not a pooled synthesis or a test of exploration alone (PDF p. 14, Figure 7 caption).

Expansion is self-reported: IdeaSynth mean = 6.05, SD = 0.89 versus baseline mean = 4.45, SD = 2.04. Figure 8 marks Expanding Research Idea with two asterisks, defined as p < 0.01 for a Wilcoxon signed-rank test treating the item independently; S1-O3.reported matches (PDF p. 13, Section 5.3.2; p. 25, Figure 8, visually inspected).

The text reports no significant individual condition differences for self-rated novelty, impact, specificity, feasibility, or relevance. Figure 8 gives no printed novelty mean or significance marker; S1-O1.reported and the numerical findings in one_line_finding match (PDF p. 15, Section 5.3.5; p. 25, Figure 8, visually inspected).

Idea-quality measures are participants' own ratings, and interaction logs measure actions rather than the creativity or diversity of produced briefs. No independent rater or computed outcome measure scores creativity/diversity of the briefs, and no across-person diversity analysis is reported (PDF pp. 12-13, Section 5.2; p. 15, Sections 5.3.4-5.3.5; p. 18, Section 7.4.2; pp. 23-25, Appendix G).

All 7 deployment participants completed the study: 3 HCI and 4 NLP, drawn from the lab sample. They were asked to use IdeaSynth for at least three days and at least one hour total, followed by a 15-30 minute interview; this is not an independent extra sample to add to the lab count (PDF p. 16, Section 6).

Core = no, criterion_2_at_least_50_people = not_met, criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output = not_met, and context_class = none are supported. No confirmed randomized study with qualifying output-scored creativity/diversity occurs in the paper; the quantitative ideation comparison is below 50 people and uses self-reports (PDF p. 4, Section 3; pp. 12-15, Section 5; p. 16, Section 6).

This is an empirical system/user-study paper rather than a synthesis; leaving the synthesis study/effect counts null and pooled estimates empty is correct (PDF p. 4, Section 3; pp. 12-16, Sections 5-6).
summary: The reported counts and self-rating statistics match the PDF, and no qualifying randomized study with creativity or diversity scored on participants' output was found. Corrections address the unsupported RCT label, omitted formative study and appendices, unverified camera-ready wording, and incomplete outcome metadata; core exclusion remains correct.
